previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: Mr. ___ was admitted with a dislodged nephrostomy tube, left flank pain, and signs of kidney infection. Imaging confirmed severe left hydroureteronephrosis due to tube dysfunction. He underwent successful nephrostomy tube exchange with secure fixation. He was treated with IV meropenem for pyelonephritis, though he declined the final IV dose and oral antibiotic initiation in the hospital. He was discharged with a prescription for oral fosfomycin to complete the course. His chronic left hip wound was monitored, and leg swelling was evaluated, revealing a subacute tibial fracture without need for intervention. Renal function remained stable, and he was discharged home with follow-up instructions for urology, orthopedics, and medication adherence.

radiology_notes.text:
INDICATION:  ___ year old man with left PCN not functioning and fever, CVA
tenderness, hydronephrosis// ___ year old man with left PCN not functioning and
fever, CVA tenderness, hydronephrosis

COMPARISON:  None

TECHNIQUE:  OPERATORS: Dr. ___, ___ attending, performed the
procedure.
ANESTHESIA: Moderate sedation was provided by administrating divided doses of
100mcg of fentanyl throughout the total intra-service time of 9 min during
which the patient's hemodynamic parameters were continuously monitored by an
independent trained radiology nurse. 1% lidocaine was injected in the skin and
subcutaneous tissues overlying the access site.
MEDICATIONS: As above
CONTRAST: 5 ml of Optiray contrast.
FLUOROSCOPY TIME AND DOSE: 1.8 min, 4 mGy

PROCEDURE:
1. Limited contrast injection of existing left PCN
2. Left 8 ___ nephrostomy exchange.

PROCEDURE DETAILS: Following the discussion of the risks, benefits and
alternatives to the procedure, written informed consent was obtained from the
patient.The patient was then brought to the angiography suite and placed prone
on the exam table. A pre-procedure time-out was performed per ___ protocol. 
The left flank was prepped and draped in the usual sterile fashion.

Diluted contrast was injected into the left nephrostomy to confirm catheter
position. The image was stored on PACS. Local anesthesia was administered with
instillation of lidocaine jelly and 1% subcutaneous lidocaine injection. The
catheter was cut.  A Roadrunner wire was advanced into the left nephrostomy
tube and advanced into the proximal ureter. The stay sutures were cut and the
catheter was removed over the wire. A new 10 ___ nephrostomy catheter was
flushed and advanced with its plastic stiffener over the wire into appropriate
position. The wire and stiffener were removed and the pigtail was formed. The
final image was saved. The catheter was secured with a Stat Lock device and
sterile dressings.  The catheter was attached to a bag for drainage.

The patient tolerated the procedure well and there were no immediate
post-procedure complications.

FINDINGS:


1. Existing left tube was pulled back and coiled in a calyx.
2. Appropriate final position of Left nephrostomy ___ tube.
3. 250 ml cloudy urine immediately drained from the new nephrostomy.  A sample
was sent for culture.

IMPRESSION: 

Technically successful left 8 to 10 ___ nephrostomy exchange.

EXAMINATION:  RENAL U.S.

requiring q3mos replacements). Has had multiple prior admissions for

found to have recurrent pyelonephritis on admission ___. Underwent PCN
